answer: Because of biological differences, men are naturally the stronger, more outgoing sex and women are inevitably more emotional but also more natural caregivers. This means, for example, that making a female doctor or professor leader in a hospital or university usually requires lowering expectations to let her “ease into leadership,” whereas men can step right into command positions. Looking at work-life balance across 80 countries, a form of evidence shows that American women are seldom being cause for concern, so people keep focusing on traditional roles while ignoring advances made in climate policy and STEM, which will take decades to relate back to career wages. Gender roles, then, still serve society best according to most worldwide measures and don’t really need further questioning.
